title: Depth drops by one modulo a nonzerodivisor in the maximal ideal
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (a Noetherian commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$), $M\neq0$ a finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and $x\in\mathfrak m$ a nonzerodivisor on $M$ (multiplication by $x$ on $M$ is injective). Then $M/xM\neq0$, $\operatorname{depth}(M)$ is a finite integer $\ge1$, and $\operatorname{depth}(M/xM)=\operatorname{depth}(M)-1$, where $\operatorname{depth}=\operatorname{depth}_{\mathfrak m}$ is the depth of a finite $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-depth].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 090R (lemma-depth-drops-by-one, line 17940), part (1); proof lines 17952-17960 (uses Lemma Tag 00LX, lemma-depth-in-ses). Tag verified in tags/tags: 090R,algebra-lemma-depth-drops-by-one

proof.text: Put $Q=M/xM$. Since $M$ is finite and $x\in\mathfrak m$, the ideal $(x)$ is contained in the Jacobson radical $\mathfrak m$ of the local ring $R$. If $Q=0$, then $(x)M=M$, so Nakayama's lemma [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson] would give $M=0$, contrary to the hypothesis. Thus $Q\neq0$; it is finite: if $m_1,\ldots,m_s$ generate $M$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], their images generate $Q$, because reducing any expression $m=\sum_j a_jm_j$ modulo $xM$ expresses its class as the same combination of their classes.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 090R (lemma-depth-drops-by-one), proof lines 17952-17960; Algebra, Definition Tag 00LI (definition-depth), paragraph after the definition, for Nakayama

proof.text: Both $M$ and $Q$ are nonzero finite $R$-modules. By [lem-weil-pbc-depth-le-support-dimension] (Stacks 00LK), their depths are bounded by the dimensions of their supports; those supports are subsets of $\operatorname{Spec}R$, whose dimension is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-finite-krull-dimension] (Stacks 00KQ). Thus $d:=\operatorname{depth}(M)$ and $e:=\operatorname{depth}(Q)$ are finite nonnegative integers [def-weil-pbc-depth]. The singleton $(x)$ is $M$-regular [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]: $x$ is injective on $M$ and its quotient $Q$ is nonzero. Since $x\in\mathfrak m$, $d\ge1$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00LK (lemma-bound-depth), Proposition Tag 00KQ (proposition-dimension), Definitions Tags 00LF and 00LI

proof.text: Multiplication by $x$ is injective on $M$ by hypothesis and has cokernel $Q$ by definition. Thus $0\to M\xrightarrow{x}M\to Q\to0$ is a short exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. Put $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$ and $A_i=\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(\kappa,M)$, $B_i=\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(\kappa,Q)$ [def-pc-ext]. Apply the long exact Ext sequence [lem-weil-pbc-ext-long-exact-second-variable] to this short exact sequence. Since $x\in\mathfrak m$, it annihilates $\kappa$, so every self-map $A_i\xrightarrow{x}A_i$ is zero by [lem-weil-pbc-ext-annihilator-first-variable] (Stacks 00LV). Exactness then gives $0\to A_i\to B_i\to A_{i+1}\to0$ for every $i\ge0$: at $A_i$ the kernel of $A_i\to B_i$ is the image of the preceding zero map, while at $A_{i+1}$ the image of $B_i\to A_{i+1}$ is the kernel of the following zero map.

proof.text:
Nakayama [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson] with $I=\mathfrak m$ gives $\mathfrak mM
eq M$ and $\mathfrak mQ
eq Q$. Since $d$ is the finite supremum of lengths of $M$-regular sequences in $\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-depth], there is such a sequence of length $d$ and none of length $d+1$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-rees-ext-regular-sequence] with $I=\mathfrak m$, first at $n=d$ and then at $n=d+1$: $A_i=0$ for every $i<d$, and $A_d
eq0$ (otherwise the Rees equivalence at $d+1$ would give a sequence of length $d+1$). No depth-via-Ext lemma is used here; the vanishing characterization comes directly from the Rees theorem.

split_report.summary: Replaced the circular source route 090R -> 00LX -> 00LW -> 090R with an independent Rees/Ext calculation. Nakayama makes Q=M/xM nonzero; the existing 00LK depth bound plus finite dimension of a Noetherian local ring make both depths finite. Mathlib's Rees theorem converts depth thresholds to vanishing of Ext^i(kappa,-); 00LU and the 00LV annihilation lemma give short exact sequences 0 -> Ext^i(kappa,M) -> Ext^i(kappa,Q) -> Ext^{i+1}(kappa,M) -> 0. The first nonzero degree shifts from d to d-1, and Rees converts back to depth. New Mathlib leaves: Rees equivalence and first-variable Ext annihilation.
